raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything too fancy. On my 3 mu, I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation the same as before. That land is small, so I can’t afford big mistakes. Wheat is our main steady crop, and maize follows right after, so I have to keep the turnaround tight. I’ve seen over the years that if wheat goes in on time in October and gets enough base fertilizer plus a topdress at jointing, it holds yield better. Maize is the same idea: don’t delay after wheat harvest, give it enough fertilizer early, and watch the rain. We have well water, but pumping costs money, so I only irrigate at the important stages. I use what is commonly available in the county, mostly improved seed, but I still manage by what worked on my own field and what nearby farmers are doing. With just 2 people in the household, I keep labor simple and rely on the usual local practice.
